outcome: Breast milk macronutrient content (protein, fat, carbohydrate, energy levels)
cohort: The study included 224 mothers (49 adolescents, 125 adults) staying at the hospital, whose gestational ages were >=37 weeks.
finding: Fat content levels in the colostrum of adolescent mothers were significantly higher compared to adult mothers, while protein and carbohydrate levels were lower in adolescents, though not statistically significant.
cross-section timing: Colostrum samples were collected from mothers postpartum.
birth_weight: Similar between adolescent and adult groups
